newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 29.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Tuesday.
- British Prime Minister John Major has again insisted that there would have to be "some decommissioning" of terrorist weapons during any future negotiations with Sinn Fein participating.

- Irish Prime Minister John Bruton was at the centre of an intensive drive to solicit donations to his political party, Fine Gael, from business people the year before he suggested to a tribunal that he was only aware of such donations on a "random basis".

- The chairman of Ireland's First National Building Society has hinted strongly at a possible flotation within the next year. - Ireland's Central Bank has again intervened to buy the Irish currency in order to prevent it losing more ground against sterling, according to market sources.
- Irish Prime Minister John Bruton hopes to meet the next British Prime Minister for talks on the peace process a week before he calls a general election in Ireland.
- Irish publicans are mounting a legal challenge to the freeze put on the price of a pint by Pat Rabbitte, Minister of State at the Department of Enterprise and Employment.

- The top-rated Wall Street fixed income sales and trading group, Bear Stearns Companies Inc., is to establish a banking operation from its new Dublin headquarters early next month. - The Irish pound fell below 95 pence sterling again on Monday as reported Central Bank selling helped it decouple from a rampant dollar and British currency.
- A 335 million Irish pound tax break, designed to cut tax on company profits by two-thirds, will form part of the Irish government's election strategy.

- New forecasts prepared by Brussels indicate that Ireland will be among the seven richest members of the EU next year. - Hopes of lifting Russian and Middle Eastern embargoes on Irish beef soared on Monday with the revelation that BSE outbreaks have fallen for the fifth successive month.
